text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Market makers want the Amsterdam stock exchange's trading system to be more open and competitive. (p1)
- Proposed merger of Holland's four electricity producers will result in the loss of 1,500 jobs. (p1)
- Government lowers 1998 tax windfall estimate from four billion guilders to two billion guilders. (p1)
- Doubling or tripling current environmental tax on energy usage would not hit economy according to government's economic policy unit CPB. (p5)
- Manufacturing sales rise four percent in May compared with a year ago. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Charter companies startled by noise reduction measures Schiphol Airport wants to impose from August 1. (p3) DE TELEGRAAF
- Conversion to Euro will cost European insurers 16 billion guilders, according to automation group Cap Gemini research. (p11)
- Suspension maker Weweler gets damages from former British customer. (p11) TROUW
- Relatives of Jewish victims of Second World War want to reclaim savings from the Postbank. (p3) --Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
